Here the combinations w-u and w-gamma^{-1}u lead to Dirichlet and Neumann Poisson problems, respectively; their required shifts need additional boundary regularity. The Fredholm argument establishes an H¹ solution, not the stronger estimate asserted for every declared domain.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the eigenvalues are sorted in ascending order based on their modulus, and when the moduli are equal, sorted in ascending order based on the size of their imaginary parts

issues.failure_explanation: Spectral convergence identifies eigenvalues inside an isolating contour, not their positions in a modulus ordering. Distinct limiting eigenvalues can have equal modulus, and arbitrarily small perturbations can reverse their modulus order regardless of the exact-spectrum imaginary-part tie-breaker. For example, limits 1+i and sqrt(2)i exchange order under outward and inward radial perturbations. Thus the indexed average need not consist of the cluster converging to lambda_j.

issues.overall_effect: The eigenvalue-average estimate and the later j-th eigenpair assertions are not justified at modulus ties between distinct eigenvalues.
issues.title: Global modulus ordering need not match convergent eigenvalue clusters
issues.why_classification: A local treatment of this degenerate indexing case preserves the cluster convergence statements and all rates without a new spectral argument.

For a defective eigenvalue their dimension can be smaller than the algebraic multiplicity q, so the displayed q-element basis and dual basis need not exist. Moreover, a split numerical Jordan cluster can span q dimensions while the exact ordinary eigenspace has smaller dimension; their symmetric gap is then 1, not a quantity tending to zero.
